articles.title: Steam Beta Defaults Non-Steam Windows Binaries to Proton
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Valve's latest Steam client beta now runs Windows binaries registered as non-Steam games through Proton by default on Linux. The update also fixes launch and stop-button issues for non-Steam games, adds a Big Picture screensaver setting, and patches a Steam Input bug.
keyPoints: Non-Steam Windows binaries now default to running via Proton
Fixed non-Steam games failing to launch after changing target binary
Big Picture can now disable the screensaver while in-game
articles.whyItMatters: Linux gamers who add Windows games to Steam manually get smoother out-of-box compatibility.

articles.title: Microsoft Releases LiteBox v0.1, a Rust-Based Sandboxing Library OS
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Microsoft has tagged the first release, v0.1, of LiteBox, its open-source Rust-based sandboxing library OS first revealed in February. LiteBox uses Linux virtualization security features to sandbox Linux apps on Linux, Linux programs on Windows, and other security-focused deployments.
keyPoints: First tagged v0.1 release of Microsoft's open-source LiteBox project
Rust-based library OS using Linux virtualization features for sandboxing
Supports sandboxing Linux apps on Linux and Linux programs on Windows
articles.whyItMatters: Developers interested in sandboxing and security isolation should note that Microsoft's Rust-based library OS is actively progressing.

articles.title: LWN.net Weekly Edition for October 8, 2026
articles.author: corbet
articles.brief: LWN's weekly edition covers kernel bugs, Gentoo's Chromium package, Rust smart pointers, the LAVD scheduler, and Python random-number modules, plus briefs on OpenSSH 10.6, Rust 1.99.0, and Zig 0.17.
articles.whyItMatters: Linux and open-source developers get a curated roundup of the week's kernel, tooling, and distribution news.

articles.title: AI-Built "Clean-Room" Rust Reimplementations of Photoshop, Premiere, Lightroom Appear
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: The ArtCraft project has released Photocraft, Filmcraft, and Lightcraft, described as AI-generated, open-source clean-room reimplementations of Adobe Photoshop, Premiere, and Lightroom written in Rust.
keyPoints: Photocraft, Filmcraft, Lightcraft mimic Photoshop, Premiere, Lightroom
Written in Rust, built predominantly with Claude Code and AI agents
Native binaries for Linux, FreeBSD, macOS, Windows; multiple releases already
articles.whyItMatters: Open-source developers and Adobe users should watch this test of whether AI clean-room clones can be credible alternatives, and of the legal questions they raise.

articles.title: A pair of flashy-looking weather extensions for GNOME Shell
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: A review of two new GNOME Shell weather extensions. Weatherglass adds animated conditions and graphed forecasts but pegs CPU and GPU even when idle. Weather Prime offers a polished, stat-packed dropdown with no API key needed, though some promised features didn't work in testing.
keyPoints: Weatherglass: animated panel icons, 8-day graphed forecast, multiple backends including Open-Meteo and NOAA
Weatherglass heavily uses CPU/GPU in the background, hurting battery life
Weather Prime: preconfigured Open-Meteo, no API key, but radar and astro features missing in practice
articles.whyItMatters: GNOME users wanting a polished panel weather applet can weigh the visual appeal against Weatherglass's resource drain and Weather Prime's uneven feature set.

articles.title: Ubuntu Summit for Ubuntu 26.10 Set for November 12-13, 2026
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: The Ubuntu Summit 26.10 event will take place on November 12-13, 2026, covering the upcoming Ubuntu 26.10 (Stonking Stingray) release. Only a teaser was available, so further details are not included.
articles.whyItMatters: Ubuntu contributors and community members can note the summit dates.

articles.title: FEX 2610 Released With AVX-VNNI Handling and Disk Cache Improvements
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: FEX 2610, the monthly release of the open-source emulator for running x86_64 games and apps on ARM64 Linux, adds AVX-VNNI support in its JIT, SSE4.2 and AVX gather optimizations, and restored 3DNow! handling. It also caps disk cache growth and fixes Vulkan thunks that help games on NVIDIA DGX Spark.
keyPoints: JIT gains AVX-VNNI support, SSE4.2 optimizations, restored 3DNow!, and RDRAND/RDSEED software fall-backs
Disk caches now have a size limit and flush on FEX updates
Vulkan thunk fixes help some games run on NVIDIA DGX Spark
articles.whyItMatters: Users running x86_64 games on ARM64 Linux, including on Valve's Steam Frame headset, get better compatibility with newer game libraries.

articles.title: IBM and Red Hat's Lightwell Fixes 400+ Previously Unknown Java Vulnerabilities
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: IBM and Red Hat report that their $5 billion Lightwell initiative has identified, remediated, and backported fixes for over 400 previously unknown vulnerabilities in widely used Java libraries. They also announced general availability of Lightwell Clearinghouse, a service letting enterprises submit dependencies for…
keyPoints: 400+ previously unknown vulnerabilities fixed and backported in Java libraries
Lightwell Clearinghouse reaches general availability for enterprise priority remediation
Fixes contributed upstream under responsible disclosure; initiative covers Linux, Kubernetes, Kafka, and more
articles.whyItMatters: Enterprise teams running older Java stacks should care, since backported fixes and priority remediation reduce exposure without forced upgrades.

articles.title: Over Half a Million Leaked GitHub Credentials Still Active, Study Finds
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Truffle Security scanned The Stack v3 dataset of 224 million GitHub repos and found 543,699 unique credentials that still authenticated, with a median exposure of 784 days and one database login valid for 16 years.
keyPoints: 543,699 unique leaked credentials still worked; oldest dated to June 2009
Push protection cut supported leaks 53%, but 51.8% of active secrets are unsupported types
Database strings rarely revoked: 88% of PostgreSQL credentials still live versus one npm token
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and security teams should treat any committed credential as compromised and rotate it immediately, since automated revocation rarely covers database or API keys.

articles.title: Podman Test Week: Help test the Rust-based conmon v3
articles.author: Petr Sklenar
articles.brief: Podman and Fedora Quality teams are running a test week October 12-18, 2026 for conmon v3, a Rust rewrite of the C container monitor used with Podman. Users install the conmon-v3 package, point Podman at it via a config drop-in, and report any behavioral differences.
keyPoints: Test week runs October 12-18, 2026; install conmon-v3 via dnf and configure conmon_path
conmon v3 replaces the C implementation with Rust for memory safety and extensible logging
Test interactive sessions, podman exec, logging, Quadlet services, rootless and rootful modes
articles.whyItMatters: Podman and Fedora users can help validate the Rust-based conmon before it becomes the default container monitor.

articles.title: Ubuntu 26.10 drops Btrfs, XFS and ZFS /boot support under Secure Boot
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Ubuntu 26.10's signed GRUB build no longer reads /boot on Btrfs, XFS, ZFS, LVM, LUKS, or non-RAID1 software RAID when Secure Boot is enabled, to shrink the pre-kernel attack surface. Affected setups will fail to boot; ext4, FAT, ISO9660 and squashfs remain supported, and disabling Secure Boot restores full GRUB…
keyPoints: Signed GRUB drops Btrfs, XFS, ZFS, LVM, LUKS, non-RAID1 RAID for /boot under Secure Boot
Aim is fewer filesystem parsers running before the kernel loads
Ubuntu 26.04 LTS keeps full GRUB for those who need it; most users unaffected
articles.whyItMatters: Ubuntu users with custom /boot layouts on Secure Boot systems should verify their setup before upgrading to 26.10.

articles.title: Star Labs StarFighter: High-End Linux Laptop With Coreboot, Core Ultra 9
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix reviews the UK-based Star Labs StarFighter, a Clevo-built 16-inch Linux laptop shipping with Coreboot and LVFS firmware updates. The review unit pairs a Core Ultra 9 285H with 64GB LPDDR5X, a 3840x2400 120Hz display, and a 1TB PCIe Gen4 SSD; AMD Ryzen 7 8845HS configs are also offered.
keyPoints: Core Ultra 9 285H (16 cores, up to 5.4GHz) with Arc Pro 140T graphics
16-inch 3840x2400 120Hz matte IPS display, 64GB LPDDR5X-7500 RAM
Coreboot firmware with LVFS/Fwupd updates; removable 1080p webcam
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users wanting a high-end, open-firmware mobile workstation get a detailed look at one of the few Coreboot-based options.

articles.title: Analyzing Rust programs with Charon
articles.author: daroc
articles.brief: Charon, from rustc pattern-matching maintainer Nadrieril, aims to make it easier to extract information from Rust crates for external tooling. It provides a stable API for accessing internal Rust compiler data.
articles.whyItMatters: Rust tooling developers who need compiler internals without relying on unstable APIs should care.

articles.title: OpenVPN 2.7.8 Released with Security and Bug Fixes
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: OpenVPN 2.7.8 is available as the eighth maintenance update to the 2.7 series, shipping bug and security fixes plus a few user-visible changes.
articles.whyItMatters: OpenVPN users should update to get the latest security fixes.

articles.title: OpenVPN 2.7.8 Released with Certificate and Windows Security Fixes
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: OpenVPN 2.7.8 fixes three security vulnerabilities, including stricter certificate validation against embedded NULL bytes and a Windows issue where cmd.exe expanded variables in quoted arguments. The release also improves DCO and server reliability, fixing errors that could terminate the whole server process.
keyPoints: Rejects certificates with embedded NULL bytes in subject fields (CVE-2026-84790)
Fixes unsigned underflow in domain_search_list and Windows cmd.exe variable expansion
DCO fixes: stale iroutes, Netlink races, and setup errors no longer kill the server
articles.whyItMatters: OpenVPN administrators, especially on Windows servers or large multi-client deployments, should update to close security holes and avoid server-wide crashes.

articles.title: NVIDIA 615.78.08 Linux Graphics Driver Improves Support for The Last of Us Part II
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: NVIDIA has released version 615.78.08 of its Linux graphics driver. The update brings bug fixes improving gaming, Wayland support, and overall driver performance.
articles.whyItMatters: Linux gamers and Wayland users on NVIDIA hardware should care about the improved game compatibility and performance.

articles.title: Vinix: a V-language, non-Linux OS that runs Docker, QEMU, and games
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: Vinix is an open-source OS with its own V-written kernel that runs Alpine Linux binaries natively by answering their system calls. It now supports Docker, QEMU, and games like DOOM and Minecraft, targeting Apple Silicon Macs, though with limits like software rendering and ARM64-only app support.
keyPoints: Runs stock Alpine Docker via its own namespaces, cgroups, overlayfs, and seccomp
Uses 50 MB RAM after boot; only M1 Macs supported so far
Limitations: no bridge networking, software emulation, ARM64 packages only
articles.whyItMatters: Developers curious about alternative kernels or lightweight macOS replacements get a working proof that Linux app compatibility doesn't require the Linux kernel.

articles.title: NVIDIA 615.78.08 Linux Driver Adds VK_NV_low_latency2 r3 for VKD3D-Proton
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: NVIDIA released the 615.78.08 Linux driver, adding VK_NV_low_latency2 revision 3 support to cut latency and stutter in VKD3D-Proton, notably with Frame Generation enabled. The release also fixes corruption in The Last of Us Part II, SELinux kernel module issues, and a crash with Vulkan HDR on Wayland.
keyPoints: VK_NV_low_latency2 r3 improves latency and stutter in VKD3D-Proton, especially with Frame Generation
Fixes blocky corruption in The Last of Us Part II and GPU page table allocation failures over 2GB
Enables NVreg_UseKernelSuspendNotifiers=1 by default for sleep/hibernation memory handling
articles.whyItMatters: Linux gamers using NVIDIA GPUs with Steam Play/Proton get lower latency and several crash and corruption fixes.

articles.title: Evolving the LAVD scheduler from gaming to servers
articles.author: corbet
articles.brief: At Kernel Recipes 2026, Changwoo Min and Gavin Guo presented the LAVD scheduler, a BPF-based extensible scheduler originally built for gaming workloads that has since expanded to other uses.
articles.whyItMatters: Developers following Linux CPU scheduling and BPF-based sched_ext may want to see how LAVD has broadened beyond its gaming origins.

articles.title: NVIDIA 615.78.08 Linux Driver Brings Vulkan Latency, Wayland Fixes
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: NVIDIA released the 615.78.08 Linux driver on its New Feature Branch, adding support for revision 3 of the VK_NV_low_latency2 Vulkan extension to cut latency and stuttering in vkd3d-proton with Frame Generation.
keyPoints: Supports VK_NV_low_latency2 revision 3 for lower latency with Frame Generation
Fixes blocky corruption in The Last of Us Part II
Fixes Wayland color-management crash from unvalidated HDR metadata
articles.whyItMatters: Linux gamers on NVIDIA GPUs and Wayland users should care, as it improves latency and fixes crashes and suspend issues.

articles.title: Raspberry Pi Desktop for x86-64 returns, now based on Debian 13
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: Simon Long announced the first new Raspberry Pi Desktop release for PCs in years, now built on 64-bit Debian 13 (trixie). The project had stalled after Bullseye due to lack of time, despite steady user demand. The move to amd64 follows Debian dropping 32-bit PC support.
keyPoints: First PC Desktop update since the Bullseye era, after repeated user requests
Switches from 32-bit to 64-bit Debian (amd64) on the trixie base
Runs on most recent PCs and Intel Macs; Apple Silicon unsupported
articles.whyItMatters: Users who run Raspberry Pi's desktop environment on old PCs or Macs finally get a current, 64-bit release.

articles.title: Security updates for Wednesday, October 7, 2026
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: LWN's daily roundup lists security updates from AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Red Hat, Slackware, SUSE, and Ubuntu. Notable packages include kernel updates for AlmaLinux, Oracle, and Ubuntu, plus sudo, freerdp, expat, openssh, and redis fixes across distributions.
keyPoints: Kernel updates for AlmaLinux 9, Oracle Linux 8, and Ubuntu 26.04 variants
sudo fixed across AlmaLinux 10 and Oracle Linux 8, 9, 10
freerdp patched in AlmaLinux, Fedora, Oracle, and Ubuntu
articles.whyItMatters: System administrators running these distributions should check for applicable patches, especially kernel, sudo, and freerdp updates.

articles.title: XOrg Server 21.1.25 and Xwayland 24.1.14 patch multiple security flaws
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: XOrg Server 21.1.25 and Xwayland 24.1.14 fix several vulnerabilities that could cause heap corruption, denial of service, or information disclosure.
articles.whyItMatters: Linux desktop users and admins running X11 or Xwayland should update to avoid the disclosed security risks.

articles.title: Kage: Google Experimenting With Linux Driver Isolation Using In-Kernel LFI Sandboxes
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Google engineers are building Kage, a Linux kernel subsystem that sandboxes device drivers using LLVM's Lightweight Fault Isolation. Sandboxed drivers keep kernel privilege but are confined to a subset of virtual memory. Prototypes using inverted VirtIO (VKage) already run NVMe, network, and WiFi drivers.
keyPoints: LFI, developed at Stanford with Google support, offers lower-overhead software fault isolation
LFI is upstream in LLVM for AArch64; x86 support targets LLVM 24
VKage prototypes sandboxed NVMe, network, and WiFi drivers
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and Android engineers should watch this as a potential path to containing buggy or malicious drivers without full virtualization overhead.

articles.title: Qualcomm Posts QPaCE Linux Driver Code For Faster ZRAM On Newest SoCs
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Qualcomm has posted Linux patches for its QPaCE hardware compression engine, found on the new Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 "Hawi" SoC, to accelerate ZRAM page compression and decompression. The initial driver adds a "qpace-lz4" Zcomp back-end targeting low-latency synchronous single-page operations.
keyPoints: QPaCE hardware accelerator appears on new Qualcomm SoCs like Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6
Patches add a "qpace-lz4" Zcomp back-end for ZRAM compressed swap
Initial driver covers only the synchronous urgent path, not asynchronous ring mode
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and users of Linux on new Qualcomm SoCs can expect faster compressed swap and lower-latency memory compression.

articles.title: Debian 14 "Forky" Artwork Proposals Are Now Open for Submission
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: The Debian Project has opened its artwork contest for the upcoming Debian 14 "Forky" release, inviting artists and designers to submit proposals for the system's desktop look and feel.
articles.whyItMatters: Designers who want to contribute to Debian can submit artwork for the next major release.

articles.title: Google Suspends Product Vulnerability Payouts in Its OSS Bug Bounty Program
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: Google has stopped accepting product vulnerability reports through its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program, calling the change temporary with an update promised in Q1 2027. Supply chain reports still pay, and reports filed before October 1 are unaffected.
keyPoints: Product vulnerability reports closed; supply chain reports remain open, paying $500 to $31,337
Google cited AI-generated submissions with hallucinated or low-impact findings
Some Google Cloud bugs may still qualify via the separate Cloud VRP
articles.whyItMatters: Security researchers reporting bugs in Google open source projects like Go, Flutter, and Angular lose a payout channel with no set return date.

articles.title: Huawei experiments with XMFS, a POSIX file-system for CXL shared memory servers
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Huawei engineers presented XMFS at LPC 2026, an experimental file-system that makes cross-node shared memory over CXL 3.0 or Huawei United Bus accessible via standard POSIX interfaces. It positions itself against FAMFS and DAXFS, with promising early benchmarks versus TMPFS.
keyPoints: Makes remote CXL 3.0 or Huawei United Bus memory addressable through POSIX file operations
Alternative to FAMFS and DAXFS; early benchmarks look promising relative to TMPFS
Tested for container image sharing and metadata-intensive workloads; still experimental
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel and server developers tracking CXL memory sharing should note a new POSIX-friendly contender, though it is far from upstream review.

articles.title: Debian Opens Artwork Call for Debian 14 "Forky"
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: The Debian Project is accepting artwork proposals for Debian 14 "Forky," expected in mid-2027. Submissions close November 26, 2026, after which the community votes on the entries. Six proposals are already listed on the Debian wiki.
keyPoints: Submission deadline is November 26, 2026, followed by a community vote
Six proposals so far, including Alborz, Cutlery, and Orange Sunshine
Themes must fit Debian style without major GTK or GDM changes
articles.whyItMatters: Debian contributors and artists can shape the next release's visual identity, and users can follow or join the vote.

articles.title: Microsoft Updates WSL2 Linux Kernel to 6.18.54.1 with DXGKRNL Fence Sharing
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Microsoft released linux-msft-wsl-6.18.54.1, rebasing its WSL2 kernel on upstream Linux 6.18.54 to pick up the latest bug and security fixes. The update adds native fence sharing for the DXGKRNL DirectX driver, re-enables DRM and VGEM support, restores PPP, and enables BPF LSM by default.
keyPoints: Kernel rebased on upstream Linux 6.18.54 for latest fixes
Native fence sharing added for DXGKRNL DirectX driver
DRM/VGEM re-enabled, PPP restored, BPF LSM on by default
articles.whyItMatters: WSL2 users, especially those relying on GPU graphics via DirectX, get improved graphics synchronization and a more secure, feature-complete kernel.

articles.title: AMD Engineer Details Zen 6 IBS Memory Profiler for Linux Hot Page Detection
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: At Linux Plumbers Conference 2026, AMD engineer Bharata Bhasker Rao presented the IBS Memory Profiler, a new Zen 6 feature for lightweight per-access memory profiling. It feeds the Linux kernel hints for hot page detection and promotion on EPYC servers with tiered DRAM/CXL memory, and benchmarks show low overhead.
keyPoints: IBS Memory Profiler tracks virtual/physical addresses and NUMA nodes per memory access
Integrates with Linux pghot patches for hot page promotion on tiered memory systems
256-core EPYC Venice benchmarks show low overhead; pghot work still ongoing
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and EPYC server operators should care, as this hardware sampling could improve memory tiering performance on future AMD systems.

articles.title: Twelve New Vulnerabilities Disclosed in X.Org Server and XWayland
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: TrendAI's Zero Day Initiative, aided by AI, disclosed twelve security vulnerabilities in the X.Org Server and XWayland. The flaws are mostly use-after-free bugs, heap buffer overflows, and out-of-bounds reads/writes. They are fixed in xorg-server 21.1.25 and xwayland 24.1.14.
keyPoints: Twelve CVEs spanning XKB, XInput, GLX, RandR, XFixes, Glamor, and Present code
Flaw classes include double free, use-after-free, heap overflows, OOB reads/writes
Fixed in xorg-server 21.1.25 and xwayland 24.1.14
articles.whyItMatters: Anyone running X11 sessions or XWayland should update, as the longstanding X.Org codebase continues to yield memory-safety bugs.

articles.title: New Zswap patches cut worst-case swap read latency from 314ms to 7ms
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Usama Arif posted two patches splitting Zswap's per-CPU compression requests so loads no longer share a mutex with stores, eliminating preemption stalls. Synchronous compressors can now decompress lock-free.
keyPoints: Stores and loads previously shared a per-CPU acomp request and mutex, causing priority-inversion stalls
Patches give loads separate requests and use lock-free on-stack requests for synchronous compressors
Slowest read fell from 314ms to 7.0ms at 8 vCPUs; mirrors earlier zRAM work by Sergey Senozhatsky
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and users of swap-heavy systems should care, since Zswap tail latency improves dramatically under contention.

articles.title: RTIPC Brings Near-Zero-Overhead Inter-Process Communication to Linux
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: RTIPC is a new Linux IPC library for hard real-time workloads, combining shared memory with a wait-free single-producer/single-consumer queue so data transfers avoid kernel copies and syscalls. It offers a formally verified 'force push' mode, cacheline-aligned messages, and optional eventfd integration, at the cost of…
keyPoints: Data path uses shared memory with no syscalls after channel setup
Force push discards oldest message when full; queue verified with SPIN/Modex
Setup exchanges file descriptors via Unix socket or D-Bus
articles.whyItMatters: Developers of latency-sensitive Linux applications get a middle ground between kernel-buffered IPC and hand-rolled shared-memory synchronization.

articles.title: Canonical Reaffirms Plans For Ubuntu 27.04 To Use ntpd-rs By Default
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Canonical reaffirmed plans to make ntpd-rs, a Rust-based, memory-safe NTP/NTS implementation, the default time synchronization package in Ubuntu 27.04. An updated ntpd-rs is available for testing in Ubuntu 26.10, whose release highlights also include Rust Coreutils, OpenSSL 4.0, Linux 7.3, and Dbus-Broker.
keyPoints: ntpd-rs targeted as default NTP implementation for Ubuntu 27.04
Updated ntpd-rs available for testing in Ubuntu 26.10 archive
Ubuntu 26.10 also ships Rust Coreutils, OpenSSL 4.0, Linux 7.3, Dbus-Broker
articles.whyItMatters: Ubuntu users and admins should care since accurate, memory-safe time sync underpins TLS validation, Kerberos, and reliable logging.

articles.title: Ubuntu 26.10 adds signed slim GRUB, TPM encryption, and VPN hardware tokens
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: Ubuntu 26.10 will add new security features: a signed, slimmed-down GRUB bootloader, TPM-backed encryption on machines lacking a hardware root of trust, and hardware-token VPN sign-in in NetworkManager.
articles.whyItMatters: Ubuntu users and admins tracking security hardening in the next release will want to know what is coming.

articles.title: Meta engineer presents AMD P-State patches boosting Steam Deck gaming at LPC
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Meta kernel engineer David Vernet presented at Linux Plumbers Conference on AMD P-State work using a per-CPU EPP boost heuristic for recently busy cores, improving frame-time tails and load times on the Steam Deck.
keyPoints: Per-CPU EPP boost for recently busy cores improves 1%-low frame rates, up to 31% earlier
Review feedback pushed design from driver heuristic to governor-level mechanism
Wine/Proton thread hints are being considered as part of the approach
articles.whyItMatters: Steam Deck and AMD Linux gamers could see better frame-time consistency and load times if this lands in the kernel.

articles.title: Red Hat's Lightwell Backports Security Fixes Without Waiting for Upstream
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: Red Hat and IBM's Lightwell backports vulnerability fixes directly into the pinned library versions enterprises actually run, instead of waiting for upstream patches. It has cleared 400 vulnerabilities in Java libraries so far, and its tailored Clearinghouse Premier tier is now generally available to any enterprise.
keyPoints: Lightwell backports fixes to pinned library versions, patching them in place
400 previously unknown Java vulnerabilities fixed; Python, JavaScript, .NET planned
Clearinghouse Premier now open to all enterprises, offering prioritized fixes and early notice
articles.whyItMatters: Enterprises stuck on unpatched legacy dependencies, especially in Java, get a way to close known vulnerabilities without upgrading versions.

articles.title: Ubuntu 26.10 Brings Rust Coreutils, OpenSSL 4.0, and a Slimmer GRUB
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Ubuntu 26.10, in beta ahead of its October 15 release, delivers sweeping security changes: a slimmed-down signed GRUB, fully Rust-based coreutils, OpenSSL 4.0, and expanded TPM disk encryption. It also switches to dbus-broker and ships kernel 7.3 with security fixes.
keyPoints: Signed GRUB drops Btrfs, ZFS, XFS drivers and LVM/LUKS /boot under Secure Boot
cp, mv, rm join uutils migration, making default coreutils entirely Rust
OpenSSL 4.0 adds Encrypted Client Hello; ENGINE and SSLv3 removed
articles.whyItMatters: Ubuntu users and admins should test scripts and Secure Boot setups before upgrading, since coreutils and GRUB changes can break existing workflows.

articles.title: NVIDIA Vera HPC benchmarks vs AMD EPYC and Intel Xeon
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix benchmarks a dual NVIDIA Vera server (176 cores, 352 threads, 1.2TB/s LPDDR5x bandwidth) on HPC workloads against AMD EPYC Turin and Intel Xeon 6 Granite Rapids systems. Testing uses NVIDIA's recommended patched Linux 6.17 stack and tracks per-test CPU power and peak frequency.
keyPoints: Dual Vera: 176 cores, 352 threads, 16x96GB LPDDR5-9600 memory
Compared with EPYC 9575F, EPYC 9755, and dual Xeon 6980P systems
Vera ran patched Linux 6.17 with 64K kernel and GCC 15.3
articles.whyItMatters: HPC buyers and admins evaluating Arm-based NVIDIA Vera systems get a rare independent comparison against current x86 flagships.

articles.title: Scrcpy 5.0 adds hardware decoding for Android mirroring
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Scrcpy 5.0 adds zero-copy hardware decoding for mirroring Android screens to a desktop, enabled by default with autodetected backends like VA-API on Linux. Benchmarks show up to a 10x drop in host CPU usage. The release also adds broader audio capture via --audio-dup and several bug fixes.
keyPoints: Hardware decoding on by default, up to 10x lower CPU usage
VA-API on Ubuntu needs the va-driver-all package; --hwdec selects a decoder
--audio-dup captures broader audio, fixing missing game audio
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users who mirror Android devices to their desktop get much lower CPU usage with no extra setup.

articles.title: Raspberry Pi OS Updated with Battery and Squeekboard Dock Widgets
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: The Raspberry Pi OS 2026-10-06 release is available for download, adding battery and Squeekboard dock widgets, Control Centre improvements, and Linux kernel 6.18.50 LTS.
articles.whyItMatters: Raspberry Pi users get new dock widgets and an updated LTS kernel in this release.

articles.title: OpenSSH 10.6 Released with Security Hardening, Post-Quantum Support
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: OpenSSH 10.6 ships security fixes, including disabling LZ77 compression to block a chosen-plaintext side-channel attack, plus hybrid post-quantum signature support. SFTP path validation is tightened, scp -R begins deprecation, and the project plans more frequent releases due to AI-assisted security bug discovery.
keyPoints: LZ77 SSH compression disabled to prevent chosen-plaintext side-channel attack
Hybrid post-quantum ssh-mldsa44-ed25519 signature enabled; WarnWeakCrypto on by default
scp -R deprecated with warning; default private key KDF rounds raised from 24 to 32
articles.whyItMatters: Anyone administering SSH servers or clients should upgrade soon and review compression, key types, and scp usage.

articles.title: Python's two modules for random numbers
articles.author: jake
articles.brief: An LWN article examines Python's random and secrets modules: both produce random values, but only secrets is suitable for passwords and security tokens. Despite long-standing misuse of random for cryptography, Python's core team added secrets in 3.6 rather than making random secure by default.
articles.whyItMatters: Python developers generating tokens or passwords should know which module is safe to use.

articles.title: Debian Trixie-Based Raspberry Pi Desktop Is Now Available for PC and Mac
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: Raspberry Pi Desktop for PC and Mac has been updated to the Debian 13 "Trixie" series, bringing the new features from Raspberry Pi OS.
articles.whyItMatters: Users running Raspberry Pi Desktop on standard PCs or Macs can now move to a Trixie-based system.

articles.title: RADV Vulkan reliability fixes land for AMD Polaris GPUs, transfer queues in progress
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Valve developer Timur Kristóf merged fixes into Mesa 26.3-devel that make Vulkan on AMD RX 400/500 "Polaris" GPUs far more reliable, enabling 20 consecutive full VK CTS runs in CI versus a 50% failure rate before.
keyPoints: Fixes merged to Mesa 26.3-devel make Polaris Vulkan more reliable
VK CTS stress test went from 50% failure to 20 clean runs
Transfer queue work lives in radv_sdma_legacy branch, needs RADV_EXPERIMENTAL=transfer_queue
articles.whyItMatters: Linux gamers and users still running decade-old AMD Polaris GPUs get more dependable Vulkan performance in Mesa.

articles.title: Last rites for Gentoo's Chromium package
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: Gentoo's maintainers are dropping the Chromium package, citing its complex build system, bundled dependencies, frequent releases, and user complaints. Chromium has long been considered one of the hardest browsers for distributions to package.
articles.whyItMatters: Gentoo users who rely on Chromium will need an alternative browser or another way to install it.

articles.title: OpenSSH 10.6 released
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: OpenSSH 10.6 enables the hybrid post-quantum ssh-mldsa44-ed25519 signature algorithm and disables the LZ77 dictionary coder to mitigate side-channel leaks, at the cost of weaker compression. It also deprecates scp -R remote-to-remote copies over security risks and adds a -p option to sftp's mkdir commands.
articles.whyItMatters: OpenSSH users and administrators should review the compression and scp changes before upgrading.

articles.title: IBM and Red Hat use AI agents to find 400+ Java vulnerabilities
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: IBM and Red Hat say their Lightwell supply-chain initiative, built on specialized AI agents, found and remediated over 400 previously unknown vulnerabilities in popular Java libraries. The announcement coincides with Lightwell Clearinghouse reaching GA, an enterprise service for priority review of open-source…
keyPoints: 400+ new vulnerabilities found in popular Java code via Lightwell AI agents
Lightwell Clearinghouse service reaches general availability for enterprise customers
IBM cites AI agents chaining low-risk flaws as a growing attack risk
articles.whyItMatters: Java developers and security teams should note the scale of AI-driven vulnerability discovery in widely used libraries.

articles.title: GNOME 52 "Terengganu" Scheduled for March 17th, 2027
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: GNOME 52, codenamed "Terengganu," now has a draft release schedule with the final release planned for March 17th, 2027.
articles.whyItMatters: GNOME users and distro maintainers can plan ahead for the desktop's next major release cycle.

articles.title: Security updates for Tuesday
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: LWN's daily roundup of Linux distribution security advisories. AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Oracle, Red Hat, Slackware, SUSE, and Ubuntu all shipped updates, with numerous kernel patches and fixes for sudo, openssh, cups, libreoffice, and many other packages.
keyPoints: AlmaLinux, Oracle, Fedora, and Ubuntu all issued multiple kernel security updates
Debian patched libreoffice, roundcube, sabnzbdplus, and ruby-oauth2
Ubuntu fixed unbound, edk2, rabbitmq-server, and aodh/watcher across releases
articles.whyItMatters: System administrators can scan this list for advisories affecting the distributions and packages they run.

articles.title: Intel shows LPMD boosts Linux gaming performance-per-Watt on Panther Lake
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: At LPC 2026 in Prague, Intel engineers presented findings on the Low Power Mode Daemon (LPMD) for Core Ultra systems. Default LPMD settings, without game-specific tuning, delivered up to an 11% performance-per-Watt gain on a Panther Lake handheld, with single-digit to low double-digit efficiency improvements across…
keyPoints: LPMD optimizes hybrid P/E/LPE core layouts on Core Ultra desktops, laptops, and handhelds
Up to 11% performance-per-Watt improvement on a Panther Lake handheld, e.g. Strange Brigade
Gains come from default LPMD configuration without per-game tuning
articles.whyItMatters: Linux gamers on Intel Core Ultra laptops and handhelds should enable LPMD for better efficiency at no tuning cost.

articles.title: Blender 6.0 May Drop OpenGL Support in Favor of Vulkan
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Blender developers are considering removing OpenGL support in Blender 6.0, targeted for November 2027, now that the Vulkan backend in Blender 5.0 has matured. No decision has been made; virtual texturing is the main blocker. Blender 5.5 LTS would be the last release for OpenGL-only platforms.
keyPoints: Internal proposal to remove OpenGL in Blender 6.0 (November 2027)
Virtual texturing is the blocker; no decision made yet
Blender 5.5 LTS would be the last option for OpenGL-only systems
articles.whyItMatters: Blender users on older hardware without Vulkan support should watch this, as it determines how long they can keep upgrading.

articles.title: aerynOS October update brings COSMIC 1.9, GNOME 51, and Budgie 10.10.3 for testing
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: aerynOS pushed a large October update to its unstable stream, including COSMIC Desktop 1.9, GNOME 51, kernel 7.2.8, Qt 6.12, and OpenSSL 4.0.3. Budgie 10.10.3 was later added to the volatile stream for testing. The project still classifies the distro as alpha quality.
keyPoints: Budgie 10.10.3 now in volatile stream for testing
Update includes COSMIC 1.9, GNOME 51, Qt 6.12, OpenSSL 4.0.3
Kernels: 7.2.8 for gaming/stable, 6.18.54 LTS; Mesa 26.2.4
articles.whyItMatters: aerynOS testers and followers of the Serpent OS successor get a broad stack refresh plus an early Budgie option.

articles.title: Meta Developing Compressed RAM "CRAM" For Linux, Faster Than ZRAM & Zswap
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Meta engineers presented Compressed RAM (CRAM) at Linux Plumbers Conference 2026, a hardware-offloaded memory compression approach for Linux. It allows cacheline/byte access to compressed memory, delivering near-native DRAM read speeds and much faster writes than ZRAM, Zswap, or swap.
keyPoints: Hardware-offloaded compression with cacheline/byte access to compressed memory
Read-only data matches raw DRAM performance; writes beat ZRAM, Zswap, and swap
Most pieces needed for CRAM support are already mainline
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users and admins facing memory shortages and high DRAM prices should care, as CRAM could expand usable memory capacity with little performance cost.

articles.title: WSL 3.0.2 adds vNUMA support for large servers and experimental sparse VHDs
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Microsoft released WSL 3.0.2, adding automatic virtual NUMA support so WSL can run on hosts with more than 256 threads, including multi-socket servers. The update also brings experimental sparse VHD creation, an IPv4 forwarding fix, and container health notifications for WSLC.
keyPoints: Automatic vNUMA support fixes WSL failing to launch on hosts with over 256 threads
Experimental sparse VHD support consumes disk space only for written data
Also fixes IPv4 forwarding and adds container health notifications to WSLC events
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and admins running WSL on large multi-socket servers can now use it reliably, and sparse VHDs can reduce disk usage.

articles.title: Intel Compiler Engineer Shares Latest Projected Gains For APX
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: At GNU Tools Cauldron 2026 in Prague, Intel and AMD engineers presented GCC enablement for APX and ACE. Intel's simulations project APX cuts loads, stores, and instructions in SPEC CPU 2017; GCC support is ready from GCC 15.1.
keyPoints: APX projects 10%+ fewer loads, 20%+ fewer stores, 10%+ fewer instructions in SPEC 2017
GCC 15.1 supports APX with Binutils 2.44+, Glibc 2.39+, Linux 6.16+; LLVM 20.1 too
AMD's ACE V1 work is landing in GCC Git, targeting GCC 17.1
articles.whyItMatters: Compiler developers and performance-focused Linux users get a preview of APX toolchain readiness and expected gains before the hardware ships.

articles.title: YSERVER 1.7 Rust X11 Server Narrows Memory Usage Difference With X.Org
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: YSERVER 1.7, a Rust-written X11 server built largely with Claude Code, cuts video memory use from 2–4GB to around 1.2GB on a 4K desktop, close to X.Org's 0.9GB. The release also speeds up CDE and Motif app startup and adds Vulkan correctness fixes.
keyPoints: vRAM use down from 2–4GB to ~1.2GB on 4K desktops, vs X.Org's ~0.9GB
Hidden windows no longer hold vRAM; GLX memory leaks fixed
CDE/Motif apps now start as fast as on X.Org via cached font look-ups
articles.whyItMatters: Developers watching Rust rewrites of X11 infrastructure get a data point on how close this alternative server is getting to X.Org parity.

articles.title: Raspberry Pi OS October 2026 Update Gets Better Dock Handling and Many Fixes
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: The October 6, 2026 Raspberry Pi OS update improves dock and taskbar handling, fixes Control Centre crashes and panel bugs, and resolves PCManFM and system tray issues. It ships with Linux kernel 6.18.50 LTS; users can update via apt full-upgrade.
keyPoints: Dock/taskbar switching no longer resets appearance; default dock adds battery and Squeekboard widgets
Ejecter plugin can auto-mount encrypted drives; automount conflict with PCManFM fixed
Ships with Linux kernel 6.18.50 LTS; update via sudo apt full-upgrade
articles.whyItMatters: Raspberry Pi desktop users get a batch of stability fixes for the panel, file manager, and tray, plus a newer LTS kernel.

articles.title: LibreSSL 4.3.3 Released with OCSP Authorization Bypass Fix
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: LibreSSL 4.3.3 is a maintenance release of the OpenBSD-developed TLS library, headlined by a fix for an OCSP responder authorization bypass in libtls and ocspcheck. It also corrects several DTLS bugs, tightens certificate verification, and improves macOS and Windows portability.
keyPoints: Fixes OCSP responder authorization bypass in libtls and ocspcheck
DTLS fixes: fragment size check, buffered handshake limit, retransmission overread
Hostname mismatch now caught even when verification callbacks always succeed
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and distro maintainers shipping LibreSSL should update to close a certificate-revocation validation flaw.

articles.title: Unofficial Firefox GNOME theme updated for Firefox 157's Nova redesign
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: The unofficial Firefox GNOME theme, a set of CSS tweaks that makes Firefox resemble native GNOME apps, has been updated to work with Firefox 157 and its rounder Nova theme. The update adapts to Nova's CSS class changes and new widget styles, keeping the Adwaita look intact.
keyPoints: Updated for Firefox 157 and the new Nova theme's CSS changes
Install via one curl script; supports binary, Flatpak, deb, RPM, Snap
Features like tabs-as-headerbar require manual about:config toggles
articles.whyItMatters: GNOME desktop users who want Firefox to match native Adwaita styling can keep the look after upgrading to Firefox 157.

articles.title: TrueNAS 27 RC.1 Released: Linux 6.18 LTS + OpenZFS 2.4
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: iXsystems released TrueNAS 27 RC.1, the first release candidate of its next major NAS operating system version, built on Linux 6.18 LTS and OpenZFS 2.4. Renamed from TrueNAS 26 to reflect its 2027 deployment, the stable release is expected in December.
keyPoints: Built on Linux 6.18 LTS kernel and OpenZFS 2.4 with AVX2 optimizations
Adds TrueSearch, WebShare, Fusion Pools 2.0, and stateful SMB failover
Early access to TrueNAS Object Interface for native S3 access to ZFS datasets
articles.whyItMatters: TrueNAS admins and homelab users should care, as this release brings performance gains, better hardware support, and new storage and sharing features.

articles.title: AMD ROCm 10.1 Released With Many Improvements
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AMD has released ROCm 10.1, continuing its six-week release cycle after ROCm 10.0 in late August. The update adds hipFILE storage improvements, NUMA-aware HIP memory allocation, beta kernel replay in ROCprofiler, a move to the LLVM 24 compiler stack, and hipThreads for incremental GPU acceleration.
keyPoints: hipFILE gains async fast-path backend, batch I/O API, and multi-tier I/O statistics
Compiler stack moves to LLVM 24 with faster rebuilds
ROCm six-week release cadence continues
articles.whyItMatters: Developers running GPU compute or AI workloads on AMD hardware should review the toolchain and performance changes.

articles.title: Hylki is a modern, Rust-based email client for GNOME
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Hylki is a new Rust-based, GTK4/libadwaita email client for GNOME, positioned as a Geary-style alternative to Thunderbird and Evolution. It offers conversation threading, multiple accounts, OpenPGP, and extensive customization, and its developer says most of the code was written by Anthropic's Claude under human…
keyPoints: Supports GNOME Online Accounts or manual IMAP/POP3, with unified inbox
Features reader mode, focus mode, Markdown composition, send-later, OpenPGP
Majority of code written by Claude LLM, reviewed and tested by a human
articles.whyItMatters: GNOME users looking for a lightweight modern mail client get a new option, and the AI-built provenance raises questions about LLM-developed desktop apps.

articles.title: mold 3.0 High-Speed Linker Released, Rewritten in Rust
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: The mold linker hit version 3.0, its first release after a full rewrite from C++ to Rust, by Rui Ueyama, author of LLVM's lld. It keeps the same options, targets, and performance, but adds bounds-checked handling of corrupted input and switches builds from CMake to Cargo.
keyPoints: First release based on the Rust rewrite; 2.42.1 is the last C++ build
Builds now require Cargo and Rust 1.95+; oneTBB dependency dropped
3.x goal: close GNU ld compatibility gaps, especially linker scripts
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and distributions relying on fast link times should note the Rust rewrite, new build requirements, and the push toward making mold a default distro linker.

articles.title: Linux 7.4 To Land New BTB CTX Isolation Feature Of AMD Zen 6
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Linux 7.4 is set to support AMD Zen 6's Branch Target Buffer Context (BTB CTX) Isolation, a hardware defense against the SRSO vulnerability. The patch, queued in tip.git's x86/bugs branch, adapts the SRSO mitigation to use this new isolation instead of SafeRET.
keyPoints: BTB CTX Isolation separates user/kernel and guest/host contexts against SRSO
SafeRET becomes unnecessary on Zen 6; IBPB covers user/user and guest/guest vectors
Patch queued in TIP branch ahead of the Linux 7.4 merge window
articles.whyItMatters: Administrators and users of upcoming Zen 6 systems should care, as this shapes how the kernel mitigates SRSO on new AMD hardware.

articles.title: Auto-cpufreq 3.2 Adds Intel HWP Dynamic Boost, Lands in Debian Repos
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Auto-cpufreq 3.2 is out, adding configurable Intel HWP Dynamic Boost (enabled by default on AC power) and Platform Profile reporting. The tool is now packaged as a .deb in Debian's official testing repositories. The release also brings battery detection fixes, GTK improvements, and Snap and power-profiles-daemon fixes.
keyPoints: Intel HWP Dynamic Boost configurable, on by default when plugged in
Now available as a .deb in Debian's official testing repos
Battery detection and GTK fixes; idna dependency bumped to 3.15
articles.whyItMatters: Linux laptop users—especially on Intel and Debian—get better power management and easier installation.

articles.title: Auto-CPUFreq 3.2 Adds Configurable HWP Dynamic Boost, Platform Profile Reporting
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Auto-CPUFreq 3.2 is out with configurable Intel HWP Dynamic Boost, now enabled by default on AC power. The release also adds more robust ACPI Platform Profile reporting and unifies system reporting with the GTK runtime state.
keyPoints: Configurable Intel HWP Dynamic Boost, enabled by default on AC power
Improved ACPI Platform Profile reporting over prior basic version
Unified system reporting and GTK runtime state for consistent view
articles.whyItMatters: Linux laptop users who rely on Auto-CPUFreq for battery life get finer control over Intel power boosting and clearer reporting.

articles.title: RustConf 2026 recordings posted
articles.author: daroc
articles.brief: The Rust Foundation has published recordings and photos from RustConf 2026, held in Montreal, Canada. LWN notes it covered four talks from the event.
articles.whyItMatters: Rust developers who missed the conference can now watch the talks online.

articles.title: An update on the Sashiko patch-review system
articles.author: corbet
articles.brief: At Kernel Recipes 2026, Sashiko maintainer Roman Gushchin explained how the LLM-based system, which automatically generates kernel patch reviews, works and how it is being improved. Sashiko has become an important part of the kernel's development process amid a persistent shortage of reviewers.
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and contributors should care, since automated review could ease the project's long-standing reviewer bottleneck.

articles.title: Siemens Takes Down OpenRadioss Repo; Community Fork OpenCourant Already Live
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: Siemens, which acquired Altair last year, abruptly deleted the OpenRadioss finite element solver repository instead of archiving it. Rocky Linux co-founder Brian Clemens has launched OpenCourant, an AGPLv3 fork with the full commit history that already ships Linux and Windows x86_64 packages.
keyPoints: Siemens deleted the OpenRadioss GitHub repo and redirected users to Simcenter Radioss.
Fork OpenCourant preserves full commit history under the same GNU AGPLv3 license.
Build pipeline was rebuilt from scratch; a rescued hm_reader binary ships in every build.
articles.whyItMatters: Engineers and researchers using the Radioss crash-simulation solver need to know the upstream is gone and where the community continuation lives.

articles.title: AMD ROCm vs. Vulkan Benchmarks for Lemonade Local AI Server With Llama.cpp
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix benchmarks AMD ROCm versus Vulkan back-ends in Llama.cpp via the Lemonade 2026.39.1 local AI server, testing a Radeon AI PRO R9700 workstation and a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 Strix Halo Framework Desktop. A year ago Vulkan was often faster than ROCm; this revisits whether that still holds.
keyPoints: Tests compare ROCm and Vulkan Llama.cpp back-ends on two AMD systems
Uses Lemonade 2026.39.1 server with Llama.cpp b10825
Hardware: Radeon AI PRO R9700 and Ryzen AI Max+ 395 Strix Halo
articles.whyItMatters: Users running local LLM inference on AMD GPUs under Linux need to know which back-end delivers better performance.

articles.title: Picard 3.0 released
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: Version 3.0 of the MusicBrainz Picard tag editor has been released. It moves to Qt6, introduces a new plugin system, and improves the user interface, cover art processing, and ISRC submission.
articles.whyItMatters: Users of the MusicBrainz Picard tag editor will want to know about the Qt6 upgrade and new plugin system.

articles.title: Security updates for Monday
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: LWN's weekly roundup lists security updates issued around October 3-5, 2026, covering AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Red Hat, SUSE, and Ubuntu. Notable fixes include Fedora updates for chromium, openssl, curl, and libX11, Debian patches for the 6.12 kernel, perl, php8.2, and xen, plus SUSE and Ubuntu advisories for…
keyPoints: Debian LTS fixes linux-6.12, perl, php8.2, pcre2, and xen
Fedora ships updates for chromium, openssl, curl, flatpak, and cri-o
Ubuntu patches ceph across 18.04 through 26.04
articles.whyItMatters: System administrators and security-conscious users should check whether any listed packages on their distributions need patching.

articles.title: Mesa Developers Looking At A Formal Governance Model
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Mesa developers are considering replacing their informal consensus approach with a formal governance council focused on conflict resolution. The idea, raised at XDC 2026 in Toronto, responds to developer burn-out; no concrete proposal exists yet.
keyPoints: Council would handle conflict resolution, not proactive decision-making
Day-to-day development would stay consensus-based
Council would arbitrate driver additions/removals, legacy support, contentious features
articles.whyItMatters: Mesa contributors and downstream Linux graphics users should care, since governance changes affect how driver and legacy-support disputes get settled.

articles.title: Linux ZRAM Rework Promises Memory Savings and Performance Gains
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Google's Sergey Senozhatsky posted a patch series reworking ZRAM's zcomp backend, splitting compression into separate per-CPU read and write streams. This fixes a priority inversion where readers block on writers' stream locks, and saves double to triple-digit KB of memory per context per CPU.
keyPoints: Read and write compression streams split so readers and writers no longer block each other
Saves tens to hundreds of KB per context per CPU, adding up across cores
Singleton recompression context saves memory with zstd, deflate, and lz4hc backends
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and users of memory-constrained systems should care, as ZRAM swap gets cheaper in memory and faster under preemption.

articles.title: Linux 7.4 to mainline Google Tensor G5 and Pixel 10 support
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A pull request for the SoC tree introduces a new ARCH_GOOGLE symbol and initial Device Tree files for the Tensor G5 (Laguna) SoC and Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, and Pixel 10 Pro XL, targeting Linux 7.4. Unlike earlier Tensor chips derived from Samsung SoCs, the G5 shares no commonality with Samsung.
keyPoints: New ARCH_GOOGLE symbol added for Tensor G5, breaking from Samsung SoC grouping
Basic support for Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, and Pixel 10 Pro XL Device Trees
G5: Cortex-X4, five A725, two A520 cores; PowerVR DXT-48-1536 GPU, 4th Gen TPU
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and enthusiasts wanting to run a mainline kernel on Pixel 10 devices can expect initial support in Linux 7.4.

articles.title: Mold 3.0 High-Speed Linker Released, Rewritten in Rust
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Mold 3.0 is out as the first release of the linker's rewrite from C++ to Rust, serving as a drop-in replacement for Mold 2.42.1. The 3.x series aims to close remaining compatibility gaps with GNU ld, especially linker script support, with the goal of becoming the default linker in Linux distributions.
keyPoints: First Rust-based release; 2.42.1 was the last C++ version
Requires Rust 1.95+, drops Intel oneTBB, builds with Cargo instead of CMake
Rust rewrite improves safety with corrupted input files and fixes many bugs
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and distro maintainers relying on fast link times should track Mold's push toward GNU ld parity and default-linker adoption.

articles.title: Phosh 0.58 Linux Mobile Shell Improves Screenshots and Flatpak Apps
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Phosh 0.58 is out with actionable screenshot notifications, a more configurable Caffeine quick setting, and better startup tracking for Flatpak and D-Bus apps. The release spans the Phoc compositor, Stevia keyboard, PFS file selector, and Phosh First Boot 0.2, and is based on GNOME 50 and wlroots 0.20.2.
keyPoints: Screenshot notifications can open the image or its folder directly
Phoc adds text-input-v3 v2 and layer-shell-effects v4 support
Stevia keyboard dictionaries can install in $HOME for immutable systems
articles.whyItMatters: Linux phone users and maintainers get usability fixes plus broader device support, including Pixel 3 XL, Pixel 9a, and Fairphone 5 tweaks.

articles.title: Linux 7.4 adds driver support for Intel's rugged Panther Lake R
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Linux 7.4 is picking up support for Panther Lake R, Intel's rugged Panther Lake variant believed to be the space-grade Starfire SoC. Patches add the new device ID to power management drivers and tools, making 7.4 the likely baseline kernel for the chip.
keyPoints: intel-uncore-freq and Intel PMC drivers gain Panther Lake R support via x86 platform drivers tree
intel_tcc_cooling driver and turbostat tool also add support
Patches mostly add the PANTHERLAKE_R device ID; 7.4 seen as baseline kernel
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and integrators targeting Intel's harsh-environment Starfire/Panther Lake R hardware should track Linux 7.4 as its first well-supported kernel.

articles.title: Qualcomm patches Linux for hardware thermal binning on Snapdragon X laptops
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Qualcomm has posted Linux kernel patches adding generic hardware-binned trip point support to the thermal framework's OF parser. The same silicon can ship in multiple thermal bins with different junction temperature limits set by manufacturing fuses, and the patches let the kernel read the correct limits, benefiting…
keyPoints: Same silicon can have different junction temperature limits set via manufacturing fuses
TSENS reads QFPROM data to decode the thermal bin before trip points are parsed
Patches are under review on the Linux kernel mailing list
articles.whyItMatters: Snapdragon X laptop users and kernel developers should care because accurate thermal limits affect throttling and performance on these machines.

articles.title: Ubuntu 26.10 Ships Rust-based Sequoia PGP, Eyes GnuPG Replacement
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: Ubuntu 26.10 preinstalls Sequoia PGP, a Rust-based OpenPGP implementation, from the main archive. Canonical's long-term goal is for it to replace GnuPG as the default toolchain, but the gpg and gpgv commands still route to GnuPG for now.
keyPoints: Sequoia PGP's sq and sqv commands are installed by default and work alongside GnuPG
Sequoia implements RFC 9580; GnuPG follows RFC 4880 and LibrePGP
Default replacement is a future goal with no announced timeline
articles.whyItMatters: Ubuntu users and packagers relying on GnuPG tooling should track this slow transition, as command routing may eventually change.

articles.title: Linux 7.4 AMD P-State driver adds Ryzen Zen 6 support
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AMD P-State driver changes queued for Linux 7.4 add initial support for upcoming Ryzen Zen 6 client CPUs, including maximum frequency capacity handling and updated EPP tuning across performance, dense, and new low-power core types.
keyPoints: amd-pstate gains max CPU frequency capacity handling for Zen 6 client processors
Updated EPP tuning covers performance, dense, and new low-power Zen 6 cores
Pull request also includes bug fixes found by the Sashiko AI agent
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users planning to buy Ryzen Zen 6 systems will want kernel 7.4 or later for proper power and frequency management.

articles.title: MAKERphone 2.0 Is an Open, Hackable 4G Phone You Build Yourself
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: CircuitMess has launched MAKERphone 2.0 on Kickstarter, a build-it-yourself 4G phone based on the ESP32-S3 that assembles in about two hours with no soldering. It makes real calls and SMS over 4G LTE Cat-1, is programmable in MicroPython or C++, and has raised over $385,000 against a $30,000 goal.
keyPoints: ESP32-S3 based phone with 4G LTE Cat-1 calls and SMS, plus Wi-Fi and Bluetooth
Assembly takes ~2 hours with no soldering; parts click, screw, or plug in
Programmable via MicroPython, C++, or AI-assisted VibeBoy environment
articles.whyItMatters: Makers and embedded hobbyists get a fully open, hackable alternative to locked-down smartphones that works as a real phone.

articles.title: Kernel prepatch 7.3-rc6
articles.author: corbet
articles.brief: Linus Torvalds released kernel 7.3-rc6, noting that the upcoming maintainer summit and Linux Plumbers Conference may change rc7 stats but shouldn't affect the release schedule.

articles.title: Linuxiac Weekly Wrap-Up: Week 40, 2026 (September 28 – October 4)
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Linuxiac's Week 40 roundup covers seven Linux distribution updates, open-source software releases, and community news from September 28 to October 4. The specific items were not included in the provided text; only section headings are visible.
articles.whyItMatters: Readers tracking weekly Linux distro and FOSS software releases get a single digest, though details require opening the full article.

articles.title: Sober runs Roblox natively on Linux without Wine
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Roblox has no official Linux support, but Sober, an unofficial runtime from the Vinegar project, runs it natively with no Wine, emulation, or virtual machines. Performance is claimed to match or beat the Windows client, though the tool is closed-source and only distributed via Flathub.
keyPoints: Sober is a native runtime for Roblox from the Vinegar project; no Wine or emulation
Requires online connection; graphics render locally with modest CPU and GPU requirements
Closed-source and Flathub-only; experimental ARM builds available via Discord
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users asked to run Roblox, or who want PC-only Roblox features natively, now have a practical option without Wine.

articles.title: 9to5Linux Weekly Roundup: October 4th, 2026
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: This week's 9to5Linux roundup covers a long list of releases, including Firefox 157, LibreOffice 26.8.1, Ubuntu 26.10 Beta, Nitrux 7.0, and Darktable 5.6.2. Only a teaser listing the covered projects was available.
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users tracking new distro and app releases get a quick overview of the week's updates.

articles.title: Linux 7.3-rc6 Released: Normal For The New "AI Normal"
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Linus Torvalds released Linux 7.3-rc6, a routine weekly RC heavy on driver fixes, with the stable 7.3 release about two weeks away. Torvalds described the churn as the new "AI normal," with many small LLM-generated error-path fixes hitting the tree and mailing lists.
keyPoints: Diffstat back to normal: roughly half the changes are driver fixes across GPU, networking, USB, sound.
Adds Turtle Beach VelocityOne Race wheel support; reverts buggy Logitech Bolt HID++ support.
Stable 7.3 expected in two weeks; maintainer summit and a vacation may affect the next merge window.
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and testers tracking 7.3 should note the AI-generated patch churn affecting review and fix timelines.

articles.title: Zig 0.17 Programming Language Lands With Reworked Build System
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Zig 0.17 is out with an expanded new ELF linker, better incremental compilation on x86_64 Linux, and a reworked build system featuring faster caching and a new Build Server Protocol for IDE integration. It also removes @cImport in favor of an external translate-c package and updates to LLVM/Clang 22.1.8.
keyPoints: New ELF linker gains full x86_64 and SPARC64 support, partial LoongArch
Incremental compilation now works with watch mode for near-instant rebuilds
Build system split into separate processes; cache 25% smaller, hits 5-10% faster
articles.whyItMatters: Zig users and systems developers tracking fast builds and cross-compilation get a significantly improved toolchain, though ZLS users face temporary breakage.

articles.title: Darktable 5.6.2 RAW Editor Fixes OpenCL Issues, Crashes, and Windows Bugs
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Darktable 5.6.2 is a maintenance release fixing OpenCL scaling on some devices, an incorrect-mask bug in Filmic RGB, and several crashes in Neural Restore, AI models, and style imports. Windows users get focus-stealing and console-window fixes, plus small memory leak and Lua scripting repairs.
keyPoints: Fixes OpenCL gamma-corrected scaling and Intel driver support
Resolves crashes in Neural Restore denoising, AI models, and malformed styles
Windows: no more focus stealing or repeated console windows for external commands
articles.whyItMatters: Darktable users, especially on Windows or with affected sensors, should upgrade—but back up first, as 5.6.x library files are incompatible with 5.4.

articles.title: Darktable 5.6.2 Adds White Balance Presets for Leica SL3-P and Sony Alpha 7R VI
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: Darktable 5.6.2, the open-source RAW image editor, is available for download with white balance presets for the Leica SL3-P and Sony Alpha 7R VI cameras, plus various bug fixes.
articles.whyItMatters: Photographers using Darktable with these cameras get out-of-the-box white balance support.

articles.title: OpenCourant: Rocky Linux team forks OpenRadioss after Siemens shutdown
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: After Siemens shut down the OpenRadioss open-source finite element solver and deleted its GitHub repository, Rocky Linux founder Brian Clemens launched OpenCourant, a community fork based on the last public snapshot.
keyPoints: Siemens closed OpenRadioss and removed its Git repository and related resources
OpenCourant forks the last public OpenRadioss snapshot under GNU AGPLv3
Fork lacks the newest binary dependencies; project seeks recent OpenRadioss binaries
articles.whyItMatters: Users of open-source crash and impact simulation software now have a community-run continuation after the original project was abruptly removed.

articles.title: MGLRU-FG patches promise 10-40% better Linux performance under memory pressure
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Kairui Song posted RFC patches adding frequency-guided promotion to Linux's MGLRU page reclaim, using per-folio access counts to proactively promote hot pages. Reported gains include 13.5% faster MongoDB, a 76% improvement in a Chromium/Node.js zRAM swap test, and faster kernel builds, though V3 has an unresolved anon…
keyPoints: Patches add access-time frequency-guided promotion to MGLRU page reclaim
10-40% higher performance or lower refault across varied tests and platforms
MongoDB 13.5% faster; zRAM swap test improved 76%; FIO up to 11% higher throughput
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and users running memory-constrained workloads should watch this, as it could significantly reduce refaults and improve performance under swap pressure.

articles.title: Pangolin 1.24 Adds Exit Nodes for Full-Tunnel VPN and Linux Subnet Routing
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Pangolin, the open-source WireGuard-based tunneled reverse proxy, released version 1.24 with Exit Nodes, upgrading it from split-tunnel to full-tunnel VPN capability. It also adds Linux Subnet Router support, letting one client expose an entire network, plus auto-connect and UI improvements across desktop and mobile…
keyPoints: Exit Nodes route all internet traffic through a site, enabling full-tunnel VPN
Automatic site selection based on latency, throughput, and availability
Linux clients can advertise a subnet so devices access resources without the client
articles.whyItMatters: Self-hosters and homelab users relying on Pangolin for secure remote access gain VPN-style full tunneling and easier LAN-wide coverage.

articles.title: ORICO X50 Review: A Sleek Thunderbolt 5 SSD Enclosure
articles.author: Abhishek Prakash
articles.brief: A hands-on review of the ORICO X50 Thunderbolt 5 NVMe enclosure on Ubuntu. It worked out of the box with full NVMe SMART data and stayed cool, but testing was capped at 40Gbps since the reviewer lacked a Thunderbolt 5 host. At $269.99 it's far pricier than USB4 alternatives.
keyPoints: Plug-and-play on Linux; drive appears as native NVMe with full SMART access
Hit 3878 MB/s read on a 40Gbps Thunderbolt 4 link; real 6000 MB/s needs TB5 host
Fanless aluminum body kept SSD at 58-68°C during a 13-minute sustained write
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users wanting fast external NVMe storage can see how it performs and whether the Thunderbolt 5 premium is justified.

articles.title: NVIDIA: Wayland and X.Org Latency Are Effectively Equal in Rigorous Testing
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: At XDC 2026, NVIDIA engineer Kamil Łysik presented end-to-end input-to-display latency measurements comparing X.Org and Wayland, using a microcontroller and light sensor on an RTX 5070 with the R610 driver. Results across KWin, Mutter, and X.Org Server were very close, with no clear winner.
keyPoints: Testing used hardware-based end-to-end measurement, from key press to presentation
XWayland no longer adds an extra frame of latency as it previously did
VRR drastically improved responsiveness with roughly equal latency on both X.Org and Wayland
articles.whyItMatters: Linux desktop users and developers debating display latency get scientific data showing Wayland is no longer slower than X.Org.

articles.title: Kagi Ends Orion Browser Development for Linux, Will Open-Source It
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Kagi is ending development of its WebKit-based Orion browser for Linux and Windows, citing limited resources. The Linux beta will keep working but stops receiving updates after October 2, 2026. Kagi plans to open-source both ports within 30 days and hopes foundations or volunteers take over maintenance.
keyPoints: Linux beta gets no updates after October 2, 2026; Kagi warns against daily use
Orion uses WebKit, a rare alternative to Chromium-based browsers
Kagi will focus on macOS and iOS, and will not maintain the open-sourced ports
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users who hoped for a non-Chromium browser option now depend on whether a community forms to maintain the released code.

articles.title: Linux Adds Workarounds for Fujitsu MONAKA CPU Bugs
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Following Fujitsu's announcement of its 144-core Arm-based MONAKA server CPU, new Linux kernel patches add CPU type detection and workarounds for three hardware bugs: faulty range-based TLB invalidation, incorrect PMU overflow detection causing interrupt storms, and a possible CPU core hang from a lost SGI.
keyPoints: Patches add MONAKA CPU type detection to enable errata workarounds
TLBI range invalidation can fail; extra TLBI instructions needed on 64K kernels
PMU overflow misdetection can trigger interrupt storms
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and early adopters of Fujitsu's Arm server hardware should track these errata before deploying MONAKA systems.

articles.title: AMD sends new GPU IP enablement and fixes to DRM-Next for Linux 7.4
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AMD submitted another AMDGPU feature pull to DRM-Next ahead of the Linux 7.4 cut-off, mostly bug fixes but including support for new hardware blocks like VPE 3.0, MMHUB 5.0, and OSSSYS 8.0.1. Updates also touch DCN 6.0, GFX12.1, HDMI 2.1, runtime power management, and AMDKFD.
keyPoints: New IP blocks: VPE 3.0, MMHUB 5.0, NBIF 7.10, SMUIO/MP 15.0.3
Additions for DCN 6.0, GFX12.1, SMU 15, plus HDMI 2.1 and runtime PM work
AMDKFD compute fixes; legacy Radeon driver gets SPARC64 and Sun XVR-300 fix
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users and developers tracking support for upcoming AMD GPUs can see early kernel enablement landing for Linux 7.4.

articles.title: openSUSE adopts ZUPT for post-quantum backups
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: openSUSE has accepted ZUPT into Factory as an officially integrated backup tool combining compression, integrity checks, and encryption. It offers AES-256 plus a hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 scheme intended to resist future quantum attacks, and uses CPU multi-threading for speed.
keyPoints: ZUPT accepted into openSUSE Factory as an officially integrated backup solution
Encryption: AES-256 plus hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 post-quantum scheme
Single tool handles backup, compression, integrity verification, and encryption with multi-threading
articles.whyItMatters: openSUSE users and admins concerned about long-term backup security against quantum threats gain a built-in, integrated option.

articles.title: DigitalOcean Quietly Ends Open Source Credits Program
articles.author: Abhishek Prakash
articles.brief: DigitalOcean is sunsetting its Open Source Credits program without any official announcement, halting new applications, renewals, and extensions. The news surfaced via a Node.js GitHub issue; after Node threatened to remove DigitalOcean branding, the company reached out about a 'version 2.0' of the program.
keyPoints: No new applications, renewals, or extensions; opensource@digitalocean.com no longer monitored
Node.js got DigitalOcean to re-engage after moving to drop its branding
DigitalOcean earlier cut GitHub Student Pack credits, also without announcement
articles.whyItMatters: Open-source maintainers relying on DigitalOcean hosting credits need to plan for paying or migrating infrastructure, with smaller projects hit hardest.

articles.title: Arm Working On "TLBID" For Linux To Increase Performance On High Core Count CPUs
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Arm posted initial Linux kernel patches for TLBI Domains (TLBID), a new architecture feature that lets TLB invalidation target only the cores a process ran on instead of the whole system. It aims to cut overhead on high core count Arm servers; no performance numbers or silicon yet.
keyPoints: TLB invalidation sent only to cores where a process ran, not system-wide
Requires LLVM 23+ or GNU Binutils 2.46+ for instruction support
Not yet in the Arm Architecture Reference Manual; silicon is far off
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and Arm server users should care, as this reduces TLB flush overhead on many-core systems.

articles.title: PhotoSuite Is a Free Photoshop-Like Editor With Native PSD Support
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: PhotoSuite is a new GPL-3.0 open-source image editor that mimics Photoshop's circa-2020 interface and uses PSD/PSB as native formats, aiming for 1:1 compatibility. Built on Tauri 2 with web technologies and Rust, it runs fully offline. Its compatibility claims are ambitious but not yet independently validated.
keyPoints: Native PSD/PSB support with layers, masks, Smart Objects, effects, and text preserved
Extensive toolset including Liquify, Lensfun correction, scripting, and Photoshop Actions playback
Tauri 2 app with DEB/RPM Linux packages, no cloud or telemetry
articles.whyItMatters: Photoshop users and Linux designers should watch it, since reliable PSD round-tripping has long been a gap in open-source graphics tools.

articles.title: Kagi ends Orion browser development for Linux, will open source the code
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Kagi has stopped developing its Orion browser for Linux, months after the GTK port entered public beta. The company cites its small team and user-funded model, and plans to open source both the Linux and unfinished Windows codebases. macOS and iOS development continues.
keyPoints: Linux beta gets no further updates; unpatched security issues expected
Kagi will open source Linux and WIP Windows ports, details within a month
Company rejected building on Chromium to preserve engine diversity
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users and open-source developers gain a potentially reusable independent browser codebase, but lose a promising native GTK browser.

articles.title: Valve's Timur Kristóf on improving old AMD GCN GPUs on Linux
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: At XDC2026 in Toronto, Valve's Timur Kristóf presented his work moving decade-old GCN 1.0/1.1 AMD cards from the legacy Radeon driver to the modern AMDGPU kernel driver. This unlocks the RADV Vulkan driver and better performance, and involved fixing display and power management issues plus adding soft reset support.
keyPoints: GCN 1.0/1.1 cards migrated from legacy Radeon to AMDGPU driver
Enables RADV Vulkan support, better performance, soft reset
Linux 6.19 saw a ~30% performance boost for these old GPUs
articles.whyItMatters: Owners of decade-old AMD GPUs and APUs get viable Linux gaming, and the talk offers a path into AMDGPU kernel development.

articles.title: Parrot OS 7.4 Released With AnonSurf 6.0 and Optimized amd64v3/arm64v8.2 ISOs
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Parrot OS 7.4, the Debian-based security distro, ships AnonSurf 6.0 rebuilt on systemd for more reliable Tor routing. It also adds a Parrot Discovery first-run setup app, CPU-optimized ISO builds, a redesigned Rocket 2.0 container manager, and refreshed security tools.
keyPoints: AnonSurf 6.0 uses systemd, adds IP/DNS checks, JSON output, Nyx support
New optimized ISOs target amd64v3 and arm64v8.2 CPU instruction levels
Rocket 2.0 gets PySide6 UI for managing containerized security tools
articles.whyItMatters: Penetration testers and privacy-focused users get more reliable Tor anonymization and faster builds on modern hardware.

articles.title: Parrot OS 7.4 Released with AnonSurf 6.0, Updated Raspberry Pi Images
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: ParrotSec released Parrot OS 7.4, the fourth update in the 7.0 series of the Debian-based penetration testing distribution. It runs Linux kernel 7.1, pulls updates from Debian 13.6 "Trixie", ships AnonSurf 6.0.1 and many updated security tools, and adds optimized x86-64-v3 ISOs plus refreshed Raspberry Pi and ARM…
keyPoints: Powered by Linux kernel 7.1 with Debian 13.6 "Trixie" package updates and patches
AnonSurf 6.0.1, Metasploit 6.5.4, and many other security tools updated
Adds x86-64-v3 optimized ISOs, Discovery setup screen, and updated ARM/Raspberry Pi images
articles.whyItMatters: Security professionals and pentesting enthusiasts using Parrot OS get a newer kernel, refreshed toolset, and better images for modern CPUs and ARM devices.

articles.title: Linux Scheduler Patches Cut Latency for Short Slice Tasks
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Linaro engineer Vincent Guittot posted an 18-patch series improving Linux scheduler latency, especially when multiple short slice tasks run concurrently. Cyclictest and Hackbench benchmarks show notable improvements, particularly in peak latency. The patches build on Guittot's recent work fixing scheduler defects.
keyPoints: 18 patches target latency with concurrent short slice tasks
Cyclictest and Hackbench show improved peak latency
Changes include decay of positive lag and slice-aware CPU selection
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and users running latency-sensitive workloads should watch these patches as they progress toward mainline.

articles.title: Rust Is Now a Tier-1 Programming Language at Microsoft
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Microsoft has made Rust a Tier-1 internal language alongside C++, C#, and TypeScript, giving teams fully supported toolchains, CI, and compliance workflows. A custom backend, rustc_codegen_utc, links rustc to MSVC's code generator for Windows interoperability.
keyPoints: Tier-1 status means Microsoft provides secure toolchains, CI, and platform integration for Rust
rustc_codegen_utc connects rustc to the MSVC backend for Windows ABI and tooling support
Backend production-ready since early 2026, self-compiling since Rust 1.90, used by 100+ repos
